pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
The daily act of Collective Worship is a legal requirement in all schools. In church schools this is Christian worship and reflects the traditions of the Church of England.
Pupils and teachers at St Paul's value the special dimension that worship brings to church school life.
Collective Worship at St Paul’s is an opportunity for the whole school to come together and reflect, express praise, share Christian values, celebrate special times throughout the year and foster respect and unity through spiritual awareness.
We begin each day with our collective worship, as a chance to come together as a whole school and set the tone for a productive and focused day ahead.
Weekly Worship Round Up
Please see our new 'Weekly Worship Round Up'. This has been created to give an overview of the themes that we are exploring in worship each week and to share some of the resources that we have been using with the children too. It is uploaded to the website on Fridays so that parents/carers can use this to support conversations at home.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Paul's C of E Primary School - Our Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Our Vision and Values
‘Enabling all to Flourish: Commitment, Courage, Love’
1 John 3:18 ‘My children, our love should be not just words and talk; it must be true love, which shows itself in action.’
Our Vision
At St Paul's, we aim to provide a safe and nurturing environment, based on our school's Christian values, where all feel confident to learn, face challenges and take risks We ensure that all are motivated, engaged and supported in becoming the best possible version of themselves - 'Enabling all to Flourish'.
Our School's Christian Values
The Bible verse found in 1 John 3:18 ‘My children, our love should be not just words and talk; it must be true love, which shows itself in action’ underpins daily life at St Paul's. Our school’s Christian values - Commitment, Courage, Love - are more than just words, they are truly lived.
Identifying and Strengthening our School's Values
During the last 5 years, our school’s vision and values have been developed and strengthened based on our lived experiences as a community.
In 2017, we began with the motto: ‘Enabling all to Flourish’ based on the Bible verse found in John 10v10: ‘I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full’. Working with the whole school community, we identified 11 positive learning behaviours that we wanted each member of our community to develop and demonstrate in their daily lives, using examples from the bible to support and strengthen understanding, and enable them to become the best possible version of themselves.
During the COVID-19 pandemic, our community wanted to strengthen this further through identification of 3 key Christian values. We spent time reflecting on our community’s response to this crisis and on 1 John 3:18 ‘My children, our love should be not just words and talk; it must be true love, which shows itself in action.’ This led us to our 3 core values: Commitment, Courage and Love.
These 3 values were (and continue to be) consistently demonstrated by our school community, supporting us in not only navigating this challenging time but in continuing to grow together. Our most recent Ofsted inspection (January 2022) highlighted that “The school’s values are an important part of daily life”.
Full Theological Underpinning Document
Exploring our Values
Whilst we promote all the gospel values, we have chosen three values that are particularly important to us and at the heart of our vision because we want all at St Paul’s to demonstrate Commitment through action and intent, to show Courage when faced with challenges and to experience Love and what that brings.
Image and Reflection created by Bella and Eliot (Year 6 Faith Reps 2021-2022)
"Commitment at St Paul’s is working hard and taking time. Commitment at St Paul’s is showing respect for our families and friends. Commitment at St Paul’s is taking part in clubs and being dedicated to jobs and roles in school."
Image and Reflection created by Louisa and Jess (Year 6 Faith Reps 2021-2022)
"Courage at St Paul’s is trying challenges and playing with people that you don’t usually play with. It’s giving everything a go. It’s important to give your best in everything and trying new things. When you think you can’t do it you need to take little steps."
Image and Reflection created by Jasmine and Kholla (Year 6 Faith Reps 2021-2022)
"Love at St Paul’s is caring for others and using kind words. It is really listening to others around you."
Living our School Values
1 John 3v18: “My children, our love should not just be words and talk; it must be true love, which shows itself in action.”
Image and Reflection created by Kyan and Obeth (Year 6 Faith Reps 2021-2022)
"God in his actions of love, courage and commitment gave us the greatest gift in his son Jesus Christ. At St Paul’s we want to show love not just in our words, but in our actions too and Jesus taught us to."
Developing Positive Learning Behaviours
We focus on the development of our 11 positive learning behaviours within all members of our community to support us all in demonstrating our school's values of Commitment, Courage and Love in all that we do. Below are some examples of how our positive learning behaviours were seen in action during our most recent Ofsted inspection (January 2022):
“Pupils are safe and feel happy in school.”
“Leaders have high expectations of pupils. They encourage pupils to take risks and learn from their mistakes.”
“Pupils behave well both in and outside of lessons. They are courteous and respectful to each other.”
“Parents and carers said the school feels like a community.”
“Pupils value the strong working relationships they have with staff and the friendships they have with their peers.”
“Through these events, leaders aim for pupils to develop skills of empathy and compassion.”
“Leaders carefully link educational visits to pupils’ learning. For instance, pupils visited The National Gallery to extend their knowledge of famous artists in art.”
“Pupils achieve well across a range of subjects.”
“Pupils are taught about children whose lives are different to their own.”
“Pupils take part in democratic activities such as voting in pupil leaders. They enjoy having areas of responsibility in school.”
“Senior leaders are reflective and continually look for improvements.”
Working in Partnership with the Community
We aim to work in partnership with parents and carers, providing workshops and other opportunities to build confidence in supporting their children at home. We ensure that our staff engage in regular training, in order to adapt and improve our approaches to education. We support our staff in continuing their own professional development and look for opportunities to work alongside other schools and professionals, providing a strong role model for our pupils of being life-long learners.
“Therefore encourage one another and build each other up, just as in fact you are doing.” 1 Thessalonians 5v11

pageCache.pageTitle: St Paul's C of E Primary School - Worship Round Up - Friday 10th July 2026
pageCache.text:
Worship Round Up
Friday 10th July 2026
Our weekly round-up aims to support our parents in the conversations that they are having at home with their children. Each week, we will share the themes of each of our worships and any resources that we have been using, such as: videos, books and music, to allow our parents to access these if they wish to. Our weekly worship is structured in the following way:
Mondays: Values worship led by Mrs Evans where each week we focus on a different school value (Commitment; Courage; Love) as a theme linking these to bible stories, quotes and our positive learning behaviours.
Tuesdays: These worships are led by Reverend Jen Houghton and will focus on the theme of ‘What God is like and what God’s kingdom is like’.
Wednesdays: These worships are led by Mrs Griffin and respond to world events and days of significance in order that we are recognising God’s presence and power in our world today.
Thursdays: Singing Assembly led by Mrs Walker.
Fridays: Celebration Worship led by class teachers. Children are rewarded for upholding our school values during the week, class and team winners are announced and a thought or reflection for the week is shared.
Monday's Worship
a Tuesday's Worship
In Tuesday’s worship Rev. Jen shared a parable about a shepherd who lost one of his one hundred sheep and would not rest until he found it. We thought about how Jesus is like a shepherd and we are his sheep and how that means that no one gets left behind or left out. We thought about how God cares for us all even if we get a little bit lost.
Wednesday's Worship
This week, we sang worship songs from our Out of the Ark Assembly collection. Many of the songs had a message of thankfulness. Through hearing a new song 'Count Your Blessings', we discussed how we could cheer ourselves up when life is difficult by noticing things we are thankful for. We sang to ask God to bless the teachers, helpers and children in our school. With the song 'Today', we sang about being grateful for every day we are given, and asked God to help us make the most of it.

Worship Round Up
Friday 11th September 2026
Our weekly round-up aims to support our parents in the conversations that they are having at home with their children. Each week, we will share the themes of each of our worships and any resources that we have been using, such as: videos, books and music, to allow our parents to access these if they wish to. Our weekly worship is structured in the following way:
Mondays: Values worship led by Mrs Evans where each week we focus on a different school value (Commitment; Courage; Love) as a theme linking these to bible stories, quotes and our positive learning behaviours.
Tuesdays: These worships are led by Reverend Jen Houghton and will focus on the theme of ‘What God is like and what God’s kingdom is like’.
Wednesdays: These worships are led by Mrs Griffin and respond to world events and days of significance in order that we are recognising God’s presence and power in our world today.
Thursdays: Singing Assembly led by Mrs Walker.
Fridays: Celebration Worship led by class teachers. Children are rewarded for upholding our school values during the week, class and team winners are announced and a thought or reflection for the week is shared.
Monday's Worship
In worship on Monday, we gathered to reflect on what it truly means to belong to the St Paul’s community. We shared stories of our summer breaks and talked about our hopes and goals for the upcoming year. Setting these goals together reminded us how working toward shared achievements strengthens our sense of belonging. To support one another, we even asked our friends to help us stay on track. We anchored our reflection in Ephesians 4:32: "Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other, just as in Christ God forgave you."
Tuesday's Worship
On Tuesday, our vicar, Jen, led a thoughtful worship all about the story of Mary and Martha. We acted out how Martha was very busy rushing around the kitchen, while her sister Mary sat quietly to listen to Jesus. Jen shared how Jesus gently reminded Martha to slow down, showing us that what Mary had chosen was important. We talked about how we can be more like Mary this year by taking quiet moments to pause, breathe, and listen carefully to each other and our learning.
Wednesday's Worship
This week, in Singing Worship, we revisited some of our harvest songs: Praise to the One, Everybody Praise Him and Everywhere Around Us. The children turned and talked to discuss why we always celebrate the harvest with a special service at this time of the year, and how we use this opportunity to give to people in need. We closed with The Lord's My Shepherd.
Thursday's Worship
In worship on Thursday, we took time to reflect on everything we have noticed around school during this first week. We shared how others have made us feel welcome and celebrated a wonderfully positive start to the term. Together, we reflected on the ways we have already shown kindness to those needing help, and we talked about our personal choices in how we treat one another. Every small action matters, and we discussed the incredible difference we can make each and every day. We anchored our reflections in Hebrews 10:24: "And let us consider how we may spur one another on toward love and good deeds."
Friday's Worship
We celebrated an amazing first week back at school firstly by finding out who won the team points this week. Then we reflected on some of the ideas that were introduced in Monday’s worship. We discussed how we can make others feel valued and welcome at school, what actions other people have done to make us feel included this week and thought carefully about how we are going to make our classrooms happy places to be next week.

pageCache.text:
Worship Round Up
Friday 12th June 2026
Our weekly round-up aims to support our parents in the conversations that they are having at home with their children. Each week, we will share the themes of each of our worships and any resources that we have been using, such as: videos, books and music, to allow our parents to access these if they wish to. Our weekly worship is structured in the following way:
Mondays: Values worship led by Mrs Evans where each week we focus on a different school value (Commitment; Courage; Love) as a theme linking these to bible stories, quotes and our positive learning behaviours.
Tuesdays: These worships are led by Reverend Jen Houghton and will focus on the theme of ‘What God is like and what God’s kingdom is like’.
Wednesdays: These worships are led by Mrs Griffin and respond to world events and days of significance in order that we are recognising God’s presence and power in our world today.
Thursdays: Singing Assembly led by Mrs Walker.
Fridays: Celebration Worship led by class teachers. Children are rewarded for upholding our school values during the week, class and team winners are announced and a thought or reflection for the week is shared.
Monday's Worship
On Monday in worship, we spent time reflecting on the importance of World Ocean Day. We started by thinking about what the Bible teaches us by looking at the following quote: "Lord, you have made many things. With your wisdom you made them all. The earth is full of your riches. Look at the sea, so big and wide. Its creatures large and small cannot be counted." Psalm 104:24-25. The Bible teaches us that we are caretakers of the earth – it is our responsibility to protect our seas, oceans and the life within them. We looked at an image of litter in the seas and oceans. We considered how we can create an impact on the world by using plastics. We then watched a story about an ant to teach us that small actions can create a huge impact. Every morning at the crack of dawn, the hardworking ant would march out of the anthill into the sprawling meadows. Ignoring the heavy morning dew, the ant would search tirelessly until he found a perfect, golden grain of wheat. Hoisting the heavy seed onto his back, the ant would make the long, arduous trek back home. Day after day, rain or shine, the ant persisted in this exact routine. He added exactly one grain to his secret pantry, knowing it would sustain his family when the ground froze. We reflected that we need to think about small actions even when it is challenges as it can create a positive ripple effect.
Tuesday's Worship
In Tuesday's worship we talked about the Parable of the Yeast and how even though yeast starts off as small and invisible it has a massive impact, we compared this to the Kingdom of God and how it will grow to transform the whole world. We thought about the qualities and values that God is helping to grow in us that will eventually have a big impact on the world.
Wednesday's Worship
In collective worship on Wednesday we focussed on awe and wonder as an important part of our spirituality. We reflected on moments when we have personally experienced this feeling, especially while watching the 'What a Wonderful World' Attenborough birthday video, which inspired us to notice beauty, kindness and connection in the world around us. Together, we reminded ourselves that spirituality can be explored through three key aspects: faith and belief, belonging and connection, and asking the big questions. These ideas helped us think more about the awe and wonder experiences we’ve had.
Thursday's Worship
This week in singing worship, we learned the rousing song, 'Shine, Jesus, Shine'. We also practised 'Faith as Small as a Mustard Seed' and the children taught Mrs Walker the actions that Jen had shown them in her recent worship. We finished our worship with 'This is Our God' and prayers.
Friday's Worship
In Friday's worship, we celebrated the team points winners for the week: Year 1 and Sapphires. We also gave out our hot chocolate awards. Then we reflected on the worships earlier in the week, thinking about how small acts that we do everyday can build up into something wonderful, if we are consistent and don't give up. We also thought about how small things can grow and can have a really big impact, even if we can't see it at first. Finally we considered one small act that we could do at school everyday next week to make our community an even nicer place to be.

pageCache.text:
Worship Round Up
Friday 15th May 2026
Our weekly round-up aims to support our parents in the conversations that they are having at home with their children. Each week, we will share the themes of each of our worships and any resources that we have been using, such as: videos, books and music, to allow our parents to access these if they wish to. Our weekly worship is structured in the following way:
Mondays: Values worship led by Mrs Evans where each week we focus on a different school value (Commitment; Courage; Love) as a theme linking these to bible stories, quotes and our positive learning behaviours.
Tuesdays: These worships are led by Reverend Jen Houghton and will focus on the theme of ‘What God is like and what God’s kingdom is like’.
Wednesdays: These worships are led by Mrs Griffin and respond to world events and days of significance in order that we are recognising God’s presence and power in our world today.
Thursdays: Singing Assembly led by Mrs Walker.
Fridays: Celebration Worship led by class teachers. Children are rewarded for upholding our school values during the week, class and team winners are announced and a thought or reflection for the week is shared.
Monday's Worship
This week, we marked Mental Health Awareness Week by exploring how to look after our minds and support those around us. We discussed simple daily habits that keep us mentally healthy, such as reading a good book, drinking plenty of water, getting enough sleep, and enjoying our favourite toys. We also learned the power of noticing things and sharing kind words to make others feel good. By linking these acts of kindness to the idea of filling buckets, we reflected on how easy it is to make someone else feel happy while filling our own buckets at the same time.
Tuesday's Worship
On Tuesday, Jen continued her series of worships where we consider the different roles that God plays in our lives (like father, strong tower or the strong/ almighty). This time, we looked at the idea of God being the one that sees us for who we are and the one who values us. We thought about the story of Hagar and Ishmael who had to leave and travel the harsh environment of the desert. God saw and heard Hagar's worries and he responded by providing water and guidance for them. We reflected on how we can all, at times, feel lonely or like we've made an error. We thought about how this was more common than we thought and that everyone has times where they do not feel seen but God is always there for us and listens to us carefully and lovingly. We finished in prayer and reflected on how God's love is unconditional and sees us and values us for who we are.
Wednesday's Worship
In worship on Wednesday we were focused on Mental Health Awareness Week, taking time to reflect on how we can care for ourselves and each other. Small actions—listening, checking in, offering kindness—help us take action and continue to fill each other’s buckets in meaningful ways. Together, we make our community stronger. We ended by asking God to help us think of others.
Thursday's Worship
This week, we began our singing worship with 'My Jesus, my Saviour'. We reflected on the story of the Good Samaritan and the fact that this story reminds us to notice those around us, even if they are not our closest friends or family. We thought about times when others have helped us and considered ways in which we can help others in our community (within our school and more widely). We closed worship with a prayer focusing on how even the smallest acts of kindness can make a difference.

On Tuesday, our vicar Jen demonstrated the meaning of generosity by filling a cup until it was overflowing with water. She explained that generosity is more than just kindness. She told the story of how Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding, making more than enough for the people to enjoy. We finished by reflecting on how we can show generosity with our thoughts, our things and our time.

In worship on Wednesday we introduced The Invisible String book. We considered how we are all connected with one another even when we are not physically with one another. We talked about the important connections we have and how through life we continue to add to these. We talked about how time and sadness can’t break, remove or destroy these connections but that we strengthen them by looking after them and giving our string an invisible tug. Please do take some time to listen to the story - your children will be able to share their reflections on how it has supported them. Invisible String Story Colossians 1:16–17: "For by him all things were created, in heaven and on earth... all things were created through him and for him. And he is before all things, and in him all things hold together."

This week in Singing Worship, we learned a new song: 'Beautiful World'. In the lyrics, we thank God for our world, for all the animals in it and for the sun and rain that helps crops to grow. We also sang 'Praise to the One' and 'Harvest Samba'. Children led us in thankful prayers and we finished with 'Here I Am, Lord'.
Friday's Worship
On Friday, we celebrated the team points and class winners for this week. Congratulations to Year 4 and Sapphires who were the team points winners for the week! We also celebrated our hot chocolate awards. We thought back to worship on Monday and recapped the meaning of 'community'. We then watched a video of the story of the Good Samaritan. We finished worship by reflecting on how we have been helped and how we have helped others this week.

Friday 19th June 2026
Our weekly round-up aims to support our parents in the conversations that they are having at home with their children. Thursdays: Singing Assembly led by Mrs Walker.
Fridays: Celebration Worship led by class teachers. Children are rewarded for upholding our school values during the week, class and team winners are announced and a thought or reflection for the week is shared.
Monday's Worship
In Monday's worship, we thought about technology. We considered the positive things that technology can do, such as helping us to communicate and connect with others and helping us to find things out and learn new things. We watched the trailer for Toy Story 5, as this new film has been created to explore the impact of technology on childhood: Toy Story 5 Trailer. After watching the trailer, we considered things that we might do more of if we did not have access to electronic devices. Some of the things we thought about were, spending more time outside, drawing, making things, playing with toys, completing jigsaws, cycling or doing other physical activities. We reflected on the message of Proverbs 4:23 "Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it." We thought the importance of taking time to put our digital devices down to experience some of the positive things that we had talked about and to ensure that we are filling our hearts with positive feelings and experiences. We talked about the announcement made that morning about the ban on certain social media apps for under 16s and the motivation of that being to guard the hearts of young people from things that do not have a positive impact. We closed worship with prayers led by the children.
Tuesday's Worship
In Tuesday's worship Reverend Jen talked about the Kingdom of God being like treasure hidden in a field. She asked two volunteers to open an envelope each, one envelope was sparkly but empty and the other was very plain but had some money inside. We thought about how the Kingdom of God can be the greatest treasure that you can find but it might not appear shiny at first. We thought about the things that we treasure and reflected on what is valuable to us.
Wednesday's Worship
This week, in singing worship, we learned a new song that the Year 6 children and staff will be singing at their Leavers Service at Southwark Cathedral in July: Ubi Caritas. This is based on a Gregorian chant from the 8th century and reminds us that where there are love and charity, there is God.
I the Lord of Sea and Sky
Thursday's Worship
On Thursday, we continued to explore the theme of Spirituality in worship. We reminded each other that spirituality is about "Faith and belief," "Belonging and connection," and "Big questions." Together, we thought about the ways in which we have felt full of faith, hope, confidence, and bravery. We also reflected on the times we have felt doubtful, unsure, worried, or questioning. To close, we reflected on the saying: “Faith helps us step forward. Doubt helps us think deeply. Together, they help us become wiser.” We then ended our worship with a prayer: "May we have the courage to ask questions, the strength to hold uncertainty, and the hope to keep growing. May we remember that faith and doubt are both part of our journey."
Friday's Worship
In Friday's worship, we celebrated the team points winners for the week: Year 3 and Rubies. We also gave out our hot chocolate awards. We revisited Monday’s worship about the positives and negatives of technology and how it shapes our week. We shared the ways we’ve used technology recently, as well as the moments we’ve stepped away from screens to enjoy the sunshine and be fully present. We ended with a reflection, each thinking of one thing we will do this weekend that doesn’t involve technology, and a prayer asking for guidance to use technology safely while making space for real connection with friends and family.

This week, our school community kicked off Walk to School Week with a vibrant and energetic whole-school assembly. The children learned all about the benefits of trading car keys for walking shoes, focusing on how a active morning commute keeps our bodies healthy and fills our brains with energy ready for learning. We also discussed the positive impact fewer cars around the school gates has on our local environment, from cleaner air to safer streets. To help us celebrate, we are running a friendly class competition throughout the week, complete with a daily travel tracker, looking at the number of pupils who walk, scoot, cycle or even "park and stride". We reflected on the importance of us all doing our part to protect the environment.
Tuesday's Worship
In Tuesday's worship we reflected on saying goodbye to people and thought about how the phrase 'goodbye' originated as a shortened form of 'God Be With You'. We then thought about Jesus' Ascension and how he said goodbye to his his disciples and encouraged them to spread the good news.
Wednesday's Worship
This Wednesday we continued with the theme of filing a bucket. We shared a video from the Boston Marathon demonstrating how we can enjoy filling others buckets and in doing so have ours filled too. We reflected on what has happen these past weeks when we have shown gratitude and shared acts of kindness. We listened to a number of children share how they have been challenging themselves with filling a bucket and different ways they have been recording these. We thanked God for one another and how we can love one another.
"A new command I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another." John 13 v 34.
Thursday's Worship
Today we were treated to a confident performance by the fabulous children in our school band, playing 'Final Countdown'. We are very proud of them. We sang, quietly, 'The Lord is my Shepherd' as we led in and out of worship. We also sang 'Seek Ye First' beautifully in two parts, 'Paul Kept the Faith' and 'Praise'.
Friday's Worship
In Friday's worship, we celebrated the team points winners for the week: Diamonds and Reception and announced the term winners - Diamonds! We recapped on what ‘walk to school week’ is all about, we then had time to discuss with our partners on how we have been making a conscious effort to walk where we can and why it’s important to do this. At the end of worship we did a vote on if we felt better for walking more and how it made us feel.

Thursdays: Singing Assembly led by Mrs Walker.
Fridays: Celebration Worship led by class teachers. Children are rewarded for upholding our school values during the week, class and team winners are announced and a thought or reflection for the week is shared.
Monday's Worship
Tuesday's Worship
On Tuesday, Reverend Jen led us in worship. We started by reflecting on who we would choose for a dinner party if we could invite anyone. We had a range of answers covering people in the past, people who were famous or our loved ones currently. Reverend Jen then shared the story of Levi the Tax collector. One day, Jesus met a man named Levi, who sat at a booth collecting tax money from the people. Many people did not like tax collectors, but Jesus looked at Levi with love and said, "Follow me." Right away, Levi left everything behind to follow Jesus! To celebrate, Levi threw a big dinner party at his house. He invited Jesus, Jesus' friends, and lots of other tax collectors and outcasts. They all sat down and ate together like a big family. Some religious leaders saw this and complained, asking why Jesus would eat with people who made mistakes. But Jesus heard them and said, "It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners. Jesus wanted everyone to know that his love is for everyone, especially those who need help finding the right path. We then considered how we could show humility and be humble in our own communities and give love to everyone even when they may not be showing love themselves. We spoke about the importance of realising that everyone is worthy of love and finished with prayers asking God to help us to love everyone.
Wednesday's Worship
In singing worship this week, we practised three songs for the harvest season: "Beautiful World", "Harvest Samba" and "Praise to the One". Children prayed to thank God for the good things in our lives.We ended our worship with an energetic rendition of "Praise".
Thursday's Worship
In worship on Thursday, we considered how our invisible strings may be different but also quite similar. The peer mentors used physical string to share their connections with one another, encouraging us all to reflect on what those connections mean for us. We looked at how many of us share similar connections and what these look like in practice. Finally, we talked about how important it is to remind ourselves of the importance of our support networks—understanding how many strings we can tug and which ones are appropriate for our varying needs. We ended by thanking God for our connections.
Friday's Worship
On Friday, we celebrated the team points and class winners for this week. Congratulations to Year 1 and Diamonds who were the team points winners for the week! We also celebrated our hot chocolate awards. We revisited Monday’s worship about generosity and how it makes us feel. After reflecting on how generosity can make a difference to us and to others, we ended with a prayer of gratitude—thanking God for all the generous people around us and asking Him to help us be generous toward others.

Monday's Worship
In Monday's worship, we thought about how much each of us 'counts' in the world. We heard about the national census taking place in India and considered the following:
- Why is it important to know how many people live in a community?
- What might happen if a whole town or group of people was completely forgotten or left uncounted?
We read Numbers 1:1-2: "The Lord spoke to Moses in the tent of meeting in the Desert of Sinai on the first day of the second month of the second year after the Israelites came out of Egypt. He said: 2 “Take a census of the whole Israelite community by their clans and families, listing every man by name, one by one." and reflected on the fact that God didn't just want a grand total number of people, he wanted them listed by name. In God's eyes, we are not just a number in a school register or a face in a crowd - we are known by name.
We then considered how it feels when someone remembers our name, says a really warm 'hello' to us and how our name can make us feel included. The Bible reminds us the importance of building a safe, fair, and welcoming world where every member is valued and we show mutual respect for one another.
Tuesday & Wednesday's Worship
On Tuesday and Wednesday, we had a great time practising a whole mix of our favourite assembly songs together. Along with all the singing, each class took time out of their day to say prayers, creating a lovely, peaceful space for everyone to reflect and give thanks.
Thursday's Worship
This week, the children sang in their classrooms. Classes could choose from our ever-expanding bank of contemporary and traditional songs. It was lovely to hear "Lord of the Dance", "Together" and "This is Our God", among others, floating along the corridor at different times throughout the week!
Friday's Worship
In Friday's worship, we celebrated the team points winners for the week: Year 2 and Diamonds. We then looked back to Monday’s worship to deepen our reflection. We revisited the concept that our name is a special part of our identity that belongs uniquely to us. We reflected on how God knows each of us individually by name and explored how being addressed by name makes us feel valued, known, and respected. We then closed worship with a prayer.
